classification.difficultyReason: Build the scaffolded table from raw marks, then select the largest count for the mode, locate the two middle positions from running totals and combine the counts that meet the probability threshold.

inlines.text: The marks obtained by 20 students in a quiz were:
Complete the following table, adding additional rows as needed.
Count each mark. Add the counts in ascending mark order to find the cumulative frequencies. Divide each count and each running total by 20 to obtain the corresponding relative frequencies.

children.label: b
children.prompt: From your table, determine the mode and median.

answer.worked:
The mark $7$ has the highest frequency, $6$, so it is the mode.

There are $20$ marks, so the middle positions are the 10th and 11th. The cumulative frequency rises from $7$ at mark $6$ to $13$ at mark $7$, so both middle marks are $7$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Median}&=\frac{7+7}{2}\\\text{Median}&=7\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Estimate the probability that a randomly chosen student scored at least $8$.

answer.worked:
Use the frequencies for marks $8$ and $9$.

$$\begin{align*}P(X\geq 8)&=\frac{5+2}{20}\\P(X\geq 8)&=\frac{7}{20}\\P(X\geq 8)&=35\%\end{align*}$$
